Sokal Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Sokal's Jewish community, first mentioned in the early 16th century, dominated local trade by the first half of the 18th century. The town was home to four Hasidic dynasties — Belz predominated, while Husiatyn, Chortkiv, and Sadigura, all documented elsewhere in this collection, were also present; some followers of the Husiatyn and Chortkiv streams later joined the Zionist movement. The ghetto's liquidation on May 27, 1943, saw about 3,000 Jews executed, following earlier deportations that sent more than 4,000 to the Bełżec death camp.
